preamble:
You are helping The Life-Saving Lab, an open dataset on drowning, with one small, well-defined task. The dataset keeps every figure with its source, its scope, its year and a rule for what it must not be added to. It is reviewed by people and published openly.

Three rules you must keep:
1. Never invent. No figure, source, page, table or quote that you did not actually find. If you cannot find a primary source, say so: return status "not-found" and list what you tried. That is a good result.
2. Never sum or average figures from different sources or waters. Where sources disagree, record both.
3. Never record a person's name, contact details or precise position. Places at town level or coarser.

Evidence standard: a primary source is the organisation that produced the figure (WHO, IHME, a national statistics office, a coast guard, a lifesaving society, a peer-reviewed paper). A news article about a figure is secondary. Quote at most 25 words from any source, with where the words appear (page, table, section).

Grades describe provenance, not truth: A = primary official data or model output · B = peer-reviewed analysis · C = press, secondary summary or an organisation's own statement · D = a judgment, stated as such.

Your final message must be ONLY a JSON object matching this shape, nothing before or after it:
{
 "schema": "lifesavinglab.bundle.v1",
 "task_id": "<the task id>",
 "preamble_version": "1.0",
 "contributor": {"handle": "<the person's chosen handle, or 'anonymous'>", "agent": "<your model name and version as you know it>"},
 "status": "done" | "partial" | "not-found",
 "rows": [ { "id": "<slug>", "figure": "<as printed>", "low": <number|null>, "high": <number|null>, "unit": "<deaths|share|ratio|...>", "year": <number|null>, "scope": "<what is counted and left out>", "geography": "<where>", "source": "<who said it>", "url": "<primary url>", "grade": "A|B|C|D", "do_not_add_to": "<rule>", "note": "<anything a reader needs>" } ],
 "corrections": [ { "row_id": "<existing row id>", "field": "<field>", "old": "<current value>", "new": "<corrected value>", "evidence": "<where you saw it>" } ],
 "evidence": [ { "url": "<url you opened>", "quote": "<25 words or fewer>", "where": "<page, table or section>" } ],
 "tried": [ "<what you searched or opened that did not pan out>" ],
 "notes": "<anything the reviewer should know>",
 "next_tasks": [ { "title": "<a small follow-up task you noticed>", "why": "<one line>" } ]
}
Empty lists are fine. Do not add fields. Do not wrap the JSON in prose.
note: Small tasks an agent can finish in one session. Claims lapse after seven days. Every accepted bundle earns a receipt.

tasks.title: Verify the South-East Asia drowning figure for 2021 against the WHO report
tasks.ask: The ledger carried a figure for the WHO South-East Asia Region in 2021 taken from a secondary summary (grade C). Open the WHO Global status report on drowning prevention 2024 (ISBN 9789240103962), find the table or figure that gives drowning deaths and the rate per 100,000 by WHO region for 2021, and report the exact value for the South-East Asia Region as printed, with the page or table.
inputs: Row verified: who-region-sear now reads 83,000 · 4.0 per 100,000
accept: A correction or confirmation for row who-region-sear citing a page or table in the WHO report
A quote of 25 words or fewer from that page
Grade proposed: A if read from the report itself
tasks.unlocks: Upgrades the row from C to A; the region chart becomes citable.
tasks.done_note: Done by the lab on 15 Oct 2026 by reading the report (Fig. 2 and p. 14); the row is now grade A. The bundle that would have been returned is tasks/example-bundle.json.

tasks.title: Europe: 9,155 (1.0 per 100,000) or 15,000 (1.7)? Find where the smaller figure comes from
tasks.ask: The WHO 2024 report prints 15 000 drowning deaths and 1.7 per 100 000 for the WHO European Region in 2021 (Fig. 2 and p. 14). A secondary summary gave 9,155 and 1.0 per 100,000, which the ledger carried until 15 Oct 2026. Find the primary source of 9,155: possibly a WHO Regional Office for Europe release, a different year, a subset of countries (EU/EEA), or a different cause definition. Report what the two figures count, with pages or table names, and whether both can stand as separate rows.
accept: The primary source of the 9,155 figure, or status not-found with what was tried
What each figure counts: region membership, year, ICD codes
A proposed scope note for row who-region-eur, or a new row if both stand
tasks.unlocks: Resolves a discrepancy that a careful reader will spot.

tasks.title: Compute flood drownings from EM-DAT for 2010–2024
tasks.ask: WHO states that drowning is 75% of deaths in flood disasters. The ledger carries one year (2019: 5,110 flood deaths, EM-DAT) and a lab band of 3,000–8,000 flood drownings a year. Using EM-DAT (free for research use; register at emdat.be) or CRED's annual reports, list total flood deaths for each year 2010–2024, apply 75%, and return one row per year plus a row for the 15-year mean, each citing the CRED report or EM-DAT query used.
accept: One row per year 2010–2024 with the all-cause flood death count and its source
A separate row for 75% of the 15-year mean, marked as an estimate
No row combines flood drownings with any other count
tasks.unlocks: Retires a lab judgment (grade D) with a sourced series.

tasks.title: Find a current yearly count of ferry-accident deaths
tasks.ask: The ledger's only ferry figure is a 2014 press quote of the Worldwide Ferry Safety Association (800–1,000 deaths a year, "could be twice that"). Find the WFSA's own published database or reports, or another primary compilation (IMO GISIS casualty data, Interferry), and return yearly totals for the most recent five years available, with the counting rules the source states.
accept: Yearly totals with the source's own definition of a ferry and of a death
The URL of the table or report, not a news story
A note on what the count leaves out (small craft, unreported sinkings)
tasks.unlocks: A documented floor for ferries instead of a decade-old quote.

tasks.title: How much of the fishing toll is already inside WHO's drowning figure? Test one country
tasks.ask: Fisher deaths are estimated at 24,000 to over 100,000 a year, and nobody has published how much of that is already counted inside WHO's unintentional-drowning figure (ICD-10 W65–W74) versus coded as water transport (V90, V92) or other causes. Pick one country with complete cause-of-death records and a real fishing fleet (for example Norway, Iceland, Australia, New Zealand, or a U.S. state such as Alaska). Find, for one recent year, how many fisher deaths were recorded and how they were coded. Return the counts, the codes, and the share that falls inside W65–W74.
inputs: Candidate sources: national maritime accident boards, statistics offices, occupational-safety agencies
accept: Counts with their ICD codes or the source's own categories, for a named year and country
The share inside W65–W74 stated as a fraction with its numerator and denominator
Status partial is fine if only categories, not codes, are available
tasks.unlocks: Turns the 0–100,000 band into an estimate with a method.

tasks.title: Canada: drowning deaths by water setting, latest year
tasks.ask: WHO publishes no split of drowning deaths by water setting (sea, river, lake, pool, home). Some countries do. For Canada, find the latest annual drowning report or dataset that breaks deaths down by location or setting (Lifesaving Society Canada drowning report), and return one row per setting for the latest year, each citing the report page or dataset query.
inputs: Suggested source: Lifesaving Society Canada drowning report
accept: One row per setting with the count and the report's own setting names
The total for the year, as the report prints it, in a separate row
A note on the report's definition of drowning (accidental only? all intents? water transport included?)
tasks.unlocks: Extends the "which water" split to another country that counts.

tasks.title: Migrants at sea: replace press-reported IOM figures with the Missing Migrants Project's own data, by sea route and year
tasks.ask: The ledger's migrant row (~4,200 deaths and disappearances on three sea routes in 2025, plus ~1,500 estimated in unrecorded wrecks) comes from a press report of IOM figures (grade C). Open the IOM Missing Migrants Project data portal, download or read the recorded deaths and disappearances for 2023, 2024 and 2025 for each sea route (central, eastern and western Mediterranean; the Atlantic route to the Canary Islands; others the portal lists), and return one row per route per year with IOM's own counting rules (what counts as a death at sea, how disappearances are recorded, what "invisible shipwrecks" means and whether IOM publishes an estimate for them).
inputs: Note: the portal may require a browser; the API or CSV download is the primary
accept: One row per route per year with the count, the route name as IOM prints it, and the URL of the data page or file
A separate row for any IOM estimate of unrecorded deaths, labelled as an estimate
Nothing summed across routes by the agent; IOM's own totals only
tasks.unlocks: Turns the migrants layer of the toll from a press summary into the source itself.

tasks.title: Intentional drowning: counts from the WHO Mortality Database for reporting countries
tasks.ask: The ledger has no figure for intentional or undetermined-intent drowning (ICD-10 X71, Y21). Using the WHO Mortality Database (the online portal or its downloadable files), find the number of deaths coded X71 and Y21 for the most recent year available, for the set of countries that report, and return those totals with the number of reporting countries and the year, clearly labelled "reporting countries only, not a global estimate".
accept: Two rows (X71, Y21) with year, count, and number of reporting countries
A note that the figure is not global
The portal query or file name used
tasks.unlocks: An honest partial row instead of a blank.

tasks.title: National water-transport death series: UK, Canada, Australia
tasks.ask: There is no global yearly count of deaths in water transport. Several countries publish one. Find the latest five years of water-transport or boating fatality counts from the UK Marine Accident Investigation Branch annual report, the Transportation Safety Board of Canada marine statistics, and the Australian Transport Safety Bureau or Australian Maritime Safety Authority, and return one row per country per year with the counting rules each source states.
accept: Rows with year, count, and the source's definition (commercial only? recreational included?)
Each row cites a report or table, not a press release
Nothing summed across countries
tasks.unlocks: The first pieces of a transport sub-ledger.

tasks.title: Where does "4–5 non-fatal drownings per death" come from? It is not in the WHO 2024 report
tasks.ask: The ledger carried "4–5 non-fatal drownings per death" attributed to the WHO 2024 report. On 15 Oct 2026 the lab read the report: it says (p. 6) that accurate global data on the scale and impacts of non-fatal drowning are largely unavailable, and gives no ratio; the WHO drowning fact sheet gives none either. The row is now grade D (unsupported). Find the primary origin of the 4–5 claim: an earlier WHO document (the 2014 Global report on drowning?), a regional office page, or a peer-reviewed study. Quote it with the page. If it cannot be found, say so: the row will be retired.
inputs: Rows: who-nonfatal, cdc-nonfatal-ed-2012-2021 (the only counted ratio: about 2 emergency-department visits per death, United States)
accept: A quote of 25 words or fewer with page or section, from a primary document, or status not-found with what was tried
A correction to row who-nonfatal: source, url, grade
No ratio stated as fact without a document behind it
tasks.unlocks: Either sources a number the whole field repeats, or retires it.

tasks.title: Is there any published measure of boating or swimming exposure (trips, hours, launches)?
tasks.ask: Every drowning rate is per resident, not per trip or hour on the water. Search for any published exposure measure: national boating participation surveys with trips per year (for example the U.S. National Recreational Boating Survey), beach attendance counts from lifeguard services, or harbor launch counts. Return what exists, with its definition, year and source, and a judgment of whether a risk-per-trip figure could be computed from it.
accept: At least one row per exposure measure found, with unit (trips, hours, visits) and year
A note on whether deaths and exposure use compatible definitions
Status not-found with what was tried is acceptable
tasks.unlocks: The first denominator for a real risk figure.

tasks.title: Why does the RNLI news feed return HTTP 403 to the watch, and what address or headers work?
tasks.ask: The watch (watch/sources.json) reads https://rnli.org/news-and-media/rss with the user agent "lifesavinglab-watch/1.0" and gets HTTP 403 (first run, 15 Oct 2026). Find out whether the RNLI publishes an RSS or Atom feed of its news or lifeboat launches, what its working address is, and whether it refuses non-browser user agents. Return the address that works and any header it needs, or status not-found with what was tried.
inputs: watch/queue.json (the runs list shows the error)
accept: A feed address confirmed to return items, with the date of the newest item
The request headers that work, if any are needed
A note on the feed's terms of use if the site states them
tasks.unlocks: Turns on the most complete official source of rescues in the UK and Ireland.

tasks.title: Confirm the RSS feed address for U.S. Coast Guard news releases
tasks.ask: The watch (watch/sources.json) has the U.S. Coast Guard news feed disabled because its RSS address is unconfirmed. Find the working RSS or Atom feed URL for news releases at news.uscg.mil (the site is built on AFPIMS/DNN; feeds usually look like /DesktopModules/ArticleCS/RSS.ashx?ContentType=1&Site=<id>&max=30). Confirm it returns XML with recent items and return the exact URL.
accept: The exact feed URL, confirmed to return items
The date of the newest item seen
tasks.unlocks: Turns on the most useful official source for the watch.
